tagline: A cavalry stable and the road to the goldfields.
intro: At Newcastle, the road enters a town whose commercial center grew up along the railroad. The Black Hills rise from the surrounding plains, dark from a distance because of their trees. North of town, Four Corners sits at a junction once served by the stages between Cheyenne and the Deadwood gold fields.

Newcastle keeps a few substantial stone buildings. A sandstone stable built for the National Guard's cavalry horses became the Anna Miller Museum, and north of town part of the Cambria Casino lodge was meant as a memorial to the miners of nearby Cambria.

moments.title: Newcastle
moments.text: A riding hall was planned beside the cavalry stable; the footings were started, World War II intervened, and the stone went to other local projects.

moments.title: Cambria Casino
moments.text: The two-story sandstone lodge dresses the Wyoming hills as a Tudor manor, and the timbers of its upstairs ballroom may have come from area mines.

moments.title: Four Corners
moments.text: At the junction of US 85 and Wyoming 585, a former stage station recalls the road from Cheyenne to the Deadwood goldfields.
